title: Examples
text: WebAssembly functions take numbers, text travels module’s memory: R writes bytes, passes pointer length, reads result back. strings.wasm works bytes place: Offset 0 fine module doesn’t use memory anything else. real module usually exports allocator; see sum.wasm example vignette("nanowasm").
code: strings <- wasm_instantiate(example_module("strings")) mem <- wasm_memory(strings)  text <- "hello from R, via WebAssembly" len <- length(charToRaw(text)) wasm_write_string(mem, 0, text, nul = FALSE)  strings$count(0L, len, utf8ToInt("o")) #> [1] 2 strings$upper(0L, len) wasm_read_string(mem, 0, len) #> [1] "HELLO FROM R, VIA WEBASSEMBLY"

title: Examples
text: mandelbrot.wasm renders Mandelbrot set memory, one byte per pixel holding number iterations point escaped. R reads bytes back matrix plots :  module arithmetic; R handles finished 43200-byte image.
code: mandel <- wasm_instantiate(example_module("mandelbrot")) w <- 240L h <- 180L maxiter <- 64L  mandel$render(0L, w, h, -2.4, -1.2, 0.9, 1.2, maxiter) iterations <- wasm_read(wasm_memory(mandel), 0, w * h, "u8") img <- matrix(iterations, nrow = w)  op <- par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0)) # Points that never escaped (the set itself) are black. colours <- c(hcl.colors(maxiter, "Inferno"), "black") image(img, col = colours, axes = FALSE, useRaster = TRUE) par(op)

title: Examples
text: module can import functions host. integrate.wasm implements trapezoidal rule imported math.f, R decides integrate: imported function can R closure, including one keeps state. counts often WebAssembly called back R: R function fails, WebAssembly call stops error carries original condition:
code: wasm_imports(example_module("integrate")) #>   module name     kind         type #> 1   math    f function (f64) -> f64  integrator <- function(f) {   wasm_instantiate(     example_module("integrate"),     imports = list(math = list(f = wasm_func(f, params = "f64", results = "f64")))   ) }  integrator(sin)$trapezoid(0, pi, 1000L) #> [1] 1.999998 integrator(dnorm)$trapezoid(-1.96, 1.96, 1000L) #> [1] 0.9500039 calls <- 0 counted_exp <- function(x) {   calls <<- calls + 1   exp(-x^2) } integrator(counted_exp)$trapezoid(-3, 3, 200L) #> [1] 1.772415 calls #> [1] 201 picky <- integrator(function(x) if (x > 1) stop("x is too large") else x) err <- tryCatch(picky$trapezoid(0, 2, 10L), nanowasm_host_error = identity) conditionMessage(err) #> [1] "The R function imported as `math.f` failed: x is too large" conditionMessage(err$parent) #> [1] "x is too large"

Anything larger, vector string, travels instance’s linear memory, byte array module reads writes pointers (byte offsets). wasm_memory() gives R view: WebAssembly standard allocator, R ask module may write. sum.wasm exports simple alloc(): type can "raw", "i8", "u8", "i16", "u16", "i32", "u32", "i64", "u64", "f32" "f64". Access of 4 bytes at offset 65534 is out of bounds of the memory (65536 bytes). end <- wasm_write_string(mem, 2048, "héllo") wasm_read_string(mem, 2048) #> [1] "héllo" wasm_global(inst, "heap_top") #> [1] 1064

code: library(nanowasm)  path <- system.file("extdata", "fib.wasm", package = "nanowasm") mod  <- wasm_module(path) mod #> <nanowasm_module> 61 bytes #> exports: #>   fib  function  (i32) -> i32 #> imports: none  inst <- wasm_instantiate(mod) inst$fib(25L) #> [1] 75025 tryCatch(inst$fib(1.5), nanowasm_argument_error = conditionMessage) #> [1] "Argument 1 of `fib` (i32) must be a whole number in [-2^31, 2^32)." inst <- wasm_instantiate(wasm_module(system.file("extdata", "sum.wasm", package = "nanowasm"))) mem  <- wasm_memory(inst)  x   <- c(1.5, 2.5, 3, 4, 5) ptr <- inst$alloc(8L * length(x)) wasm_write(mem, ptr, x, "f64") inst$sum_f64(ptr, length(x)) #> [1] 16 inst <- wasm_instantiate(mod, limits = wasm_limits(memory = 16 * 2^20, timeout = 1)) inst$fib(45L) #> Error in inst$fib(45L) : #>   The WebAssembly call was stopped after 1 second, its time limit. mod <- wasm_module(system.file("extdata", "log.wasm", package = "nanowasm")) log <- wasm_func(function(ptr, len, caller) {   message(wasm_read_string(caller$memory(), ptr, len)) }, params = c("i32", "i32"))  inst <- wasm_instantiate(mod, imports = list(env = list(log = log))) inst$greet() #> Hello from WebAssembly!

title: Conditions signalled by nanowasm — nanowasm-conditions
text: Every error nanowasm raises class nanowasm_error, plus specific class code can catch tryCatch():

title: Conditions signalled by nanowasm — nanowasm-conditions
text: nanowasm_invalid_object: object longer points live module instance, example saveRDS() / readRDS() round trip. nanowasm_validation_error: bytes valid WebAssembly module. nanowasm_link_error: module instantiated imports given. missing field lists missing imports. nanowasm_argument_error: value passed R fit function's signature. subclass nanowasm_precision_error used i64 result represented exactly double. nanowasm_unsupported: function uses type nanowasm pass R WebAssembly (funcref, externref, v128). nanowasm_trap: WebAssembly code trapped. trap_id names trap ("div_by_zero", "unreachable", "out_of_bounds_memory_access", ...) detail holds interpreter's message. Subclasses: nanowasm_stack_exhausted (call value stack limit) nanowasm_out_of_bounds (memory table access bounds). nanowasm_memory_limit: instance reached memory limit (see wasm_limits()), interpreter allocate memory. nanowasm_timeout: call ran longer time limit. elapsed limit seconds. nanowasm_reentry_error: instance called already running call. nanowasm_runtime_error: failure inside interpreter. --bounds wasm_read() wasm_write() calls signal nanowasm_out_of_bounds , subclass nanowasm_argument_error. Pressing Ctrl-C call signals R's usual interrupt condition.

title: Resource limits for an instance — wasm_limits
text: memory caps everything interpreter allocates instance: linear memories, tables, globals stacks running calls. memory.grow exceed fails inside WebAssembly (returning -1, specification requires). allocation exceed signals nanowasm_memory_limit error. frames maximum call depth, stack maximum number value-stack cells (4 bytes ). Exceeding either signals nanowasm_stack_exhausted error. timeout wall-clock time single call (including start function instantiation) may run, seconds. Exceeding signals nanowasm_timeout error. checked every 50 milliseconds execution. Pressing Ctrl-C (Esc) interrupts running call regardless limits, R code. call stopped limit interrupt may leave instance's memory globals partly updated. instance stays usable, whether state still makes sense depends module.

title: Access an instance's linear memory — wasm_memory
code: wasm_memory(instance, name = NULL)  wasm_read(memory, offset, n, type = "u8")  wasm_write(memory, offset, x, type = "u8")  wasm_read_string(memory, offset, n = NULL)  wasm_write_string(memory, offset, x, nul = TRUE)  wasm_memory_size(memory, unit = c("bytes", "pages"))  wasm_memory_grow(memory, pages)

title: Access an instance's linear memory — wasm_memory
text: instance nanowasm_instance. name export name memory. default, NULL, picks instance's exported memory. memory nanowasm_memory wasm_memory(). offset Byte offset (0-based). n Number elements read. wasm_read_string(), number bytes, NULL read first NUL byte. type Element type; see Details. x wasm_write(), vector write. wasm_write_string(), single string. nul Whether write terminating NUL byte string. unit Report size "bytes" "pages" (64 KiB ). pages Number pages add.

title: Access an instance's linear memory — wasm_memory
text: wasm_memory() returns nanowasm_memory. wasm_read() returns vector length n wasm_read_string() string. wasm_write() wasm_write_string() invisibly return offset just past bytes written. wasm_memory_size() returns number, wasm_memory_grow() previous size pages.

title: Access an instance's linear memory — wasm_memory
text: Offsets 0-based byte addresses, numbers WebAssembly function receives pointers, 1-based R indices. Every access checked memory's current size; one falls outside signals nanowasm_out_of_bounds error changes nothing. type gives element type, stored little-endian WebAssembly requires: Writes check every element changing memory: integer types reject NA, fractions values outside type's range. WebAssembly standard allocator. pass data function, use module's allocation export (often named malloc alloc) get offset, write .

title: Access an instance's linear memory — wasm_memory
code: mod <- wasm_module(system.file("extdata", "sum.wasm", package = "nanowasm")) inst <- wasm_instantiate(mod) mem <- wasm_memory(inst) mem #> <nanowasm_memory> `memory`: 1 page (64 KiB)  # Ask the module for room for 5 doubles, fill it, and sum it. x <- c(1.5, 2.5, 3, 4, 5) ptr <- inst$alloc(8L * length(x)) wasm_write(mem, ptr, x, "f64") inst$sum_f64(ptr, length(x)) #> [1] 16 wasm_read(mem, ptr, 5, "f64") #> [1] 1.5 2.5 3.0 4.0 5.0  next_free <- wasm_write_string(mem, 1024, "héllo") wasm_read_string(mem, 1024) #> [1] "héllo" wasm_read(mem, 1024, next_free - 1024, "u8") #> [1] 104 195 169 108 108 111   0

title: Load a WebAssembly module — wasm_module
code: path <- system.file("extdata", "add.wasm", package = "nanowasm") mod <- wasm_module(path) mod #> <nanowasm_module> 66 bytes #> exports: #>   add      function  (i32, i32) -> i32 #>   add_f64  function  (f64, f64) -> f64 #> imports: none  wasm_validate(path) try(wasm_validate(as.raw(1:8))) #> Error in wasm_validate(as.raw(1:8)) :  #>   Invalid WebAssembly module: wrong magic: 4030201.

title: nanowasm 0.0.0.9000
text: Development version, heading first release (0.1.0). wasm_module() loads validates WebAssembly module raw vector .wasm file; wasm_validate() checks . wasm_exports() wasm_imports() list module provides needs. wasm_instantiate() creates instance (running start function), wasm_call() inst$name(...) calls exported functions, converting i32, i64, f32 f64 values R. wasm_memory() gives access instance’s linear memory: wasm_read() / wasm_write() typed vectors, wasm_read_string() / wasm_write_string() UTF-8 strings, wasm_memory_size() / wasm_memory_grow(). wasm_global() reads sets exported globals. Modules can import R functions: wrap wasm_func() pass wasm_instantiate(imports = ). R function caller argument can reach calling instance’s memory. wasm_limits() bounds instance’s memory, call depth, value stack time per call; Ctrl-C interrupts running call. Every failure classed condition (nanowasm_trap, nanowasm_timeout, nanowasm_host_error, …); see ?nanowasm-conditions. Modules run bundled toywasm interpreter (v76.0.0), system WebAssembly runtime needed. vignette("nanowasm") walks API, example modules add.wasm, fib.wasm, sum.wasm log.wasm installed extdata/.
